summary: The HotGauge paper (W4205499638) presents a methodology for characterizing thermal hotspots in advanced processors across 14nm, 10nm, and 7nm technology nodes using co-simulation of Sniper (performance), McPAT v1.2 (power), and 3D-ICE v3.0.0 (thermal). The scenario describes a 7-core out-of-order processor with SMT, running single-threaded SPEC2006 benchmarks at 5 GHz and 1.4 V (turbo boost), with 200M instruction ROI and transient thermal simulation. The paper validates dynamic power (Cdyn) against Intel Core i5-10310U (14nm; 11% error) and Core i7-1165G7 (10nm; 20% error), then extrapolates the 7nm model without real silicon validation. Key findings include: 7nm reaches hotspots 5× faster than 14nm for gcc, peak MLTD of ~70°C in 7nm versus <60°C in 14nm, and time-to-hotspot (TUH) ranging 0.2–150 ms across SPEC2006 benchmarks. Studio run was blocked due to missing floorplan geometry (no x,y coordinates or block dimensions) and absence of per-functional-unit power traces in the input specification.
limitations: Experiment classified as not_2d_applicable: The scenario specifies a custom_2d_steady run but provides no floorplan blocks (0 of 1–128 required) and no power_w object; 3D-ICE thermal model and transient dynamics (1M cycle time steps) inherently 3D, not reducible to 2D steady-state analysis.

Missing critical input data: No published floorplan coordinates, functional unit dimensions (mm), or per-block power dissipation time series; paper references Fig. 5 schematic and Table I microarchitecture only, lacking quantitative layout geometry necessary for block-level thermal mapping.

Power model validation gap at 7nm: McPAT v1.2 Cdyn validated to ±11–20% at 14nm/10nm only; 7nm extrapolation unvalidated against real silicon, amplifying uncertainty in thermal predictions for the primary case study.

Floorplan scaling assumption mismatch: Paper assumes uniform 50% area reduction per node (14nm 5 mm²→10nm 2.5 mm²→7nm 1.25 mm²) but acknowledges that real die size remains roughly constant with logic density increase; global wire delay scaling not proportional to area, creating timing-thermal coupling inconsistency not fully characterized.

Non-uniform temperature initialization qualitative only: Background OS thermal state modeled as idle warmup but exact initialization conditions not specified; sensitivity of hotspot metrics (Tth=80°C, MLTDth=25°C, σ sigmoid parameters) to initial condition choice not quantified.

Single-threaded workload scope: SPEC2006 run single-threaded on one core; SMT (2 threads/core) and multi-core contention effects omitted from primary analysis, limiting generalizability to realistic multi-threaded deployment scenarios.

Repository and artifact validation incomplete: GitHub URL and Zenodo DOI (10.5281/zenodo.5523504) cited but not independently verified; exact Sniper version, 3D-ICE build configuration, McPAT XML config, and SPEC2006 binary compilation flags not disclosed.

Thermal stack model excludes solder balls and motherboard: 3D-ICE simulates silicon through heatsink but omits PCB and packaging parasitics; contact resistance between thermal grease/TIM and heatsink not quantified, affecting Ψ j,a thermal resistance accuracy (14nm 0.96 °C/W, 10nm 1.13 °C/W, 7nm 1.4 °C/W).

Hotspot severity metric calibration undisclosed: Three sigmoid functions (σdf, σM, σT) parameterized from 'industry data' (Equations 2, page 6) but source data, calibration methodology, and sensitivity analysis not provided; critical threshold σ=0.5 selection rationale not justified.

Deterministic gate constraint: Input validation errors (missing blocks, power_w object) and blocking facts (evidence locator mismatches, no asset downloads) prevent Studio execution; comparison_valid=false, so no numerical replication claim is valid.

-Area scaling 50% per technology node (14nm→10nm→7nm) with constant floorplan layout and core placement
-Dynamic power (Cdyn) decreases 20% per technology node following transistor scaling trends
-Leakage power and area scaled to match advanced nodes using standard transistor scaling assumptions
-Frequency fixed at 5 GHz (turbo boost V-f point) and voltage at 1.4 V across all process nodes
-Heatsink model HS483-ND with fan at 6000 rpm remains identical across technology nodes; die area reduction increases thermal resistance Ψ per node
-Hotspot definition parameterized: Tth=80°C (max junction minus margin), MLTDth=25°C (timing slack), radius=1mm (global wire delay in clock cycle)
-Hotspot severity metric composed of three parameterized sigmoid functions calibrated from industry data: σdf (device failure at 115°C), σM and σT (timing margins with non-linear temperature effects)
-Background thermal state initialized with idle OS workload trace prior to ROI to model realistic multi-tasking environment
-Cache warm-up performed before 200M instruction ROI simulation; transient thermal dynamics captured with 1M cycle time steps
-Floorplan inspired by Intel Skylake; 50 functional units modeled compared to 6 units in prior HotSniper work
